prompt: A team says its system has no architecture because nothing was ever designed on purpose. What is the course's answer?

choices.text: Then it has none until somebody documents it
choices.why: A document describes an architecture; it does not create one.

choices.text: It has one; nobody is deciding it
choices.why: Right: structure exists whether chosen or not, and the risk is that it accumulates by accident.

choices.text: It has a design but not an architecture
choices.why: Accidental decisions with high cost of change are architecture whatever their origin.

choices.text: Its architecture is the framework it uses
choices.why: A framework is a technology; lesson 2 separates it from the structure built with it.

prompt: Two services exchange orders. A designer replaces the HTTP call between them with a table both read and write, to avoid timeouts. What changed, in the course's terms?

choices.text: Nothing architectural, since the boxes are the same
choices.why: Same boxes, different connector: a different architecture with different failures.

choices.text: Coupling went down, since there is no call any more
choices.why: Coupling moved into the schema, where every column change now involves both teams.

choices.text: The architecture: timeouts traded for coupling through the schema
choices.why: Right: a shared table removes the call failing and adds hidden coupling and lock contention.

choices.text: Only the technology, from HTTP to SQL
choices.why: The technology changed, but so did who knows about whom and what fails together.

prompt: A request passes through four services in a synchronous chain, each available 99.5% of the time. To one decimal place, what percentage of the time does the chain work?
hint: Lesson 1: availabilities in a chain multiply.

prompt: A payments company must show auditors, years later, the exchange rate used in each transfer. Which force of the environment is this, and what does it become?

choices.why: Right: the same shape as ANTT's floor table — keep what was in force when the decision was made.
On-call follows from running the system, not from what auditors ask for.

choices.text: The organisation, becoming a team split
choices.why: No team structure is involved; the requirement comes from outside the company.

choices.text: The business, becoming a performance target
choices.why: Speed is not what auditors ask for; they ask for evidence.

prompt: By Booch's definition, a design decision is architectural when it is significant, and significance is measured by its cost of ___.
A company has six teams and one shared service that all of them must change for most features. A year later, the teams queue to deploy it. What does the course call this?

choices.why: Deploying is where it shows, but the cause is a structure at odds with the teams.
Nothing here was chosen for careers; it is a shared component against a team structure.
That concept is about when to decide; this is about a structure bending to the organisation.

choices.text: Conway's law, bending the structure back
choices.why: Right: a structure that ignores the organisation is bent back into its shape, here as a queue of teams.
